$$

feedback.problem:
Given that the mean of the following data set is $4,$ find the value of $z:$ 

$$
2,\,z,\,z,\,6,\,9,\,z,\,2
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the mean is denoted by $\overset{―}{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}
$$

Here, there are $n=7$ data points. Adding up all the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i} & =2+z+z+6+9+z+2 \\  & =19+3z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mean is given by the expression

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (19+3z) \\  & =\frac{19+3z}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we're told that $\overset{―}{x}=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =\frac{19+3z}{7} \\ 28 & =19+3z \\ 9 & =3z \\ z & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
